sentences.text:
The prayers in this Writ Petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India are as follows:-
"(i) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ directing the respondent nos. 2 to 6 to issue notice of appearance to the petitioner under Section 35(3) of the Lintomon K.T vs The State Of Kerala on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152538456/
2 Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, in all pending and future crimes arising out of the same transaction;
(ii) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, directing the respondent nos. 2 to 6 to properly comply the directions in Arnesh Kumar v State of Bihar and Anr. (2014) 8 SCC 273 and Sathendar Kumar Antil v. CBI and Anr. (2022) 10 SCC 51 and provisions of the Section 35 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 if there are any circumstances that warrant the arrest of the petitioner.

sentences.text: And (iii) Such other relief's as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the circumstances of the case."

2.The petitioner is the accused in a series of crimes alleging offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the 2026:KER:9975 WP(CRL.) NO. 203 OF 2026 Indian Penal Code and Sections 316(2), 318, 115(2) and 126(2) r/w Section 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, registered by different police stations across the State of Kerala.

3.The petitioner seeks a blanket order directing respondents 2 to 6 to issue notices under Section 35(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita in all pending and future cases arising out of the same transaction.
4.The learned Public Prosecutor resisted the application and contended that the blanket protection as prayed for cannot be granted.

5. As per Section 35(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita,"the police officer shall, in all cases where the arrest of a person is not required under sub-section (1) issue a notice directing the person against whom a reasonable complaint has been made, or credible information has been received, or a reasonable suspicion exists that he has committed a cognizable offence, to appear before him or at such other place as may be specified in the notice"
6.

The learned Public Prosecutor submitted that e ach case registered against the petitioner is being independently 2026:KER:9975 WP(CRL.) NO. 203 OF 2026 and separately considered to determine whether the provisions of Section 35(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita are applicable.
The pleadings are very vague and therefore insufficient to seek the reliefs prayed for.
Therefore, the writ petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
